assignments.title: 🔥 Particle Motion Lab: Build a State of Matter Model
assignments.html:
🔥 Particle Motion Lab: Build a State of Matter Model


📜 Standard:
SC.7.P.11.1 – Recognize that adding heat to or removing heat from a system may result in a temperature change and possibly a change of state.

🎯 Objective
In this investigation, you will build a 3D physical model that shows how heat affects particle motion and the states of matter.

 

Scientists often use models to help visualize how particles behave in solids, liquids, and gases. Because particles are too small to see directly, models help us understand how heat energy changes the movement of particles.

 

Your model will help demonstrate:

• How heat affects particle motion
• The difference between solid, liquid, and gas particle movement
• How adding or removing heat can change the state of matter

 

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

• Represent particle motion in solids, liquids, and gases
• Show how adding heat increases particle movement
• Show how removing heat decreases particle movement
• Identify examples of changes of state

🔥 Mission Briefing

ALL matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.

The amount of motion depends on how much heat energy is present.

 

When heat is added or removed, particles move differently.

 

In a solid, particles vibrate in place and stay tightly packed together.

In a liquid, particles still stay close together but can slide past each other.

In a gas, particles move quickly and spread far apart.

 

Heat energy changes how particles move, and this motion determines the state of matter.

When enough heat is added or removed, matter can change state.

 

Examples include:

• Evaporation / Boiling – liquid → gas
• Condensation – gas → liquid
• Freezing – liquid → solid

 

Scientists use particle models to explain these changes.

 

Your mission is to build a particle motion model that shows how heat affects the states of matter.

🧰 Your Task

Using materials you can find around your house, build a 3D particle motion model that shows the three states of matter.

 

⚠️ This assignment MUST be a 3D physical model made with materials.
It should NOT be a drawing or diagram on paper.

 

Your model should show:

• Particles in a solid
• Particles in a liquid
• Particles in a gas

 

You may use materials such as:

• Beads or small balls
• Clay or playdough
• Rice or beans
• Cotton balls
• Bottle caps or small objects
• Cardboard or containers
• Recycled materials

 

Your materials should clearly represent particles and how they move in each state of matter.

⭐ What Your Model Must Show

Your model must include three sections representing the states of matter.

 

🧊 Solid

Show:

• Particles packed closely together
• Very little space between particles
• Particles vibrating in place

 

Label and explain:

• Low particle motion
• Low energy

💧 Liquid

Show:

• Particles still close together
• Particles able to slide past each other

 

Label and explain:

• Medium particle motion
• Medium energy

💨 Gas

Show:

• Particles far apart
• Particles moving freely

 

Label and explain:

• High particle motion
• High energy

🔥 Heat and Changes of State

Your model must also have labels that explain examples of heat being added or removed.

 

Include labels for:

• Evaporation or boiling (liquid → gas)
• Condensation (gas → liquid)
• Freezing (liquid → solid)

 

Use arrows and labels to show how heat causes these changes.

⭐ Model Requirements

Your 3D particle model must include and clearly label:

• Solid particle arrangement
• Liquid particle arrangement
• Gas particle arrangement
• Particle motion differences
• Heat being added or removed
• Changes of state

 

All features must include labels and short explanations.

📸 Photo Requirement

Take clear photos of your completed particle model.

 

You may submit as many photos as needed to clearly show:

• The three states of matter
• Particle motion differences
• Labels and explanations
• Heat causing state changes

 

Multiple photos are encouraged if they help make your model easier to understand.

📊 Rubric

Category Points What This Means
Accurate particle model 12 Model correctly represents particle arrangements in solids, liquids, and gases.
Representation of heat and state changes 10 Model clearly shows how heat affects particle motion and state changes.
Scientific labels and clarity 8 All required features are labeled and explained clearly.

💯 This Assignment is worth 30 Points.

assignments.title: 🔥➡️❄️ Heat Transfer Mission: Restore Thermal Equilibrium
assignments.html:
🔥➡️❄️ Heat Transfer Mission: Restore Thermal Equilibrium

📜 Standard:
SC.7.P.11.4 – Observe and describe that heat flows in predictable ways, moving from warmer objects to cooler ones until they reach the same temperature.

🎯 Objective

In this assignment, you will build a VR model that demonstrates heat transfer and thermal equilibrium.

Heat is a form of energy that moves between things when there is a temperature difference. Heat always moves in a predictable direction: from warmer to cooler.

 

This movement happens because particles in warmer materials move faster than particles in cooler materials. When they interact, the faster-moving particles transfer energy to the slower-moving particles.

 

As energy transfers, temperatures begin to change. The warmer item cools down while the cooler item warms up.

 

Eventually, both reach the same temperature. When this happens, heat transfer stops. This state is called thermal equilibrium.

 

In this activity, you will use VR modeling to demonstrate how heat moves and how balance is eventually reached.

 

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

Explain the direction of heat transfer

Model how heat moves from warmer to cooler

Demonstrate how temperatures change over time

Explain what happens when thermal equilibrium is reached

🌌 Mission Briefing

Your VR simulation has detected an energy imbalance.

 

Two things in your environment have very different temperatures. One is much warmer, while the other is much cooler. Because of this difference, energy immediately begins to move.

 

Heat always flows in one direction:

Warm → Cool

 

As heat transfers:

• The warmer item begins to cool down
• The cooler item begins to warm up

 

This process continues until both reach the same temperature.

When this happens, the system reaches thermal equilibrium.

 

At equilibrium:

• Heat is no longer transferring between them
• Temperatures are equal
• The system becomes balanced

 

Your mission is to build a VR environment that clearly demonstrates how heat moves and how equilibrium is restored.

 

Anyone exploring your world should be able to clearly see how heat travels from warmer to cooler areas and how balance is eventually reached.

🧰 Your Task

You will build a heat transfer demonstration inside a 360° environment from the IFX Gallery.

Step 1 — Choose a 360° Environment

1️⃣ Enter ENGAGE VR

2️⃣ Open the IFX Gallery

3️⃣ Load a 360° environment from the IFX library

 

You may choose any environment you want, as long as you can clearly demonstrate heat transfer within it.

 

Examples might include:

• A kitchen or dining area
• An outdoor environment
• A science lab
• A campsite or outdoor scene
• A classroom environment

 

Your environment will become the setting for your heat transfer demonstration.

Step 2 — Create a Temperature Difference

Choose two things that clearly have different temperatures.

 

Examples could include:

• A hot cup of soup and a metal spoon
• Ice melting in your hand
• A hot drink sitting on a table
• A cold can warming in the sun

 

One should represent the warmer temperature and the other the cooler temperature.

 

This temperature difference is what causes heat transfer to begin.

Step 3 — Show the Direction of Heat Transfer

Add arrows in your VR environment to show the direction heat is moving.

 

Your arrows should clearly demonstrate:

Warm → Cool energy movement

 

The arrows should make it easy for viewers to see how heat travels between the two items.

Step 4 — Show Thermal Equilibrium

Demonstrate what happens when the temperatures eventually become the same.

 

At this point:

• Heat transfer stops
• Both reach thermal equilibrium
• Temperatures become balanced

 

Your environment should clearly show how the situation changes from heat transfer to equilibrium.

Step 5 — Label Key Concepts

Use sticky notes to label and explain the science happening in your environment.

 

Required labels:

Warmer Temperature

Cooler Temperature

Thermal Equilibrium

 

Each sticky note should include a short explanation of what is happening.

🌎 Required Components

Your VR environment must clearly show:

✔ A warmer temperature and a cooler temperature

✔ Arrows showing the direction of heat movement

✔ Temperature change occurring over time

✔ Thermal equilibrium where temperatures become equal

✔ Sticky note explanations describing each concept

 

Someone exploring your environment should be able to clearly understand how heat moves and how equilibrium is reached.

📸 Submission Requirement — VR Photos

To submit this assignment, upload photos taken inside your VR environment.

You must submit as many photos as necessary so that each sticky note label can be clearly read.

 

Your photos should show:

• The warmer and cooler temperatures
• The arrows showing direction of heat movement
• The labeled explanation notes
• The final state of thermal equilibrium

 

Make sure your screenshots are clear and readable.

⏰ In-Class Work Requirement & After-School Policy

This assignment will be built during scheduled class time in VR.

You are expected to enter VR and actively work during the assigned class period.

 

If you missed class, arrived late, or chose not to enter VR with the class, you must complete the entire assignment during the after-school VR session.

If you did not finish during class, you must also complete the remaining work during that after-school session.

 

The VR access code is posted in your Canvas Announcements page.

Choosing not to participate during class does not remove the requirement to complete the assignment.

📊 Rubric

Category Points What This Means
Accurate demonstration of heat transfer 10 Heat clearly moves from warmer areas to cooler areas.
Clear explanation of thermal equilibrium 8 Labels explain how equilibrium is reached.
Complete and organized VR environment 6 The environment clearly demonstrates the heat transfer process.
Clear photos showing labels and model 6 Submitted photos clearly show the model and readable labels.

 

💯 This assignment is worth 30 Points.

assignments.title: 📡⚡ Breaking News: The Law of Conservation of Energy
assignments.html:
📡⚡ Breaking News: The Law of Conservation of Energy

📜 Standard:

SC.7.P.11.3- Cite evidence to explain that energy cannot be created nor destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

🎯 Objective

In this assignment, you will create a VR breaking news broadcast explaining the Law of Conservation of Energy.

 

Energy is involved in nearly every change that occurs in the universe. Whenever something moves, produces heat, gives off light, or creates sound, energy is involved.

Energy can exist in many forms, including thermal energy, light energy, sound energy, electrical energy, chemical energy, and mechanical energy. These different forms of energy can change from one form into another through processes called energy transformations.

 

Scientists have discovered an important rule about energy called the Law of Conservation of Energy. This law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed. Instead, energy can only be transferred from one object to another or transformed from one form into another.

 

Even when energy seems to disappear, it has actually changed form or moved somewhere else in the system.

For example, when a flashlight turns on, chemical energy stored in the battery changes into electrical energy, which then produces light and heat. The energy was not created—it simply changed form.

 

By studying how energy moves and changes forms, scientists can better understand how systems work.

In this assignment, you will act as a news reporter inside a VR news studio and produce a short breaking news broadcast explaining how the Law of Conservation of Energy works in real-world situations.

 

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

• Define energy as the ability to cause change or do work
• Explain the Law of Conservation of Energy
• Identify examples of energy transfer
• Identify examples of energy transformation
• Explain how energy changes forms while remaining conserved

🌌 Mission Briefing

Scientists have confirmed an important discovery about how energy behaves.

 

According to the Law of Conservation of Energy, energy cannot be created or destroyed. Instead, energy can only move between objects or change from one form into another.

This means the total amount of energy in a system remains constant, even when energy transformations occur.

 

For example, when a moving object slows down, it may seem like the energy of motion has disappeared. In reality, some of that energy has been transformed into thermal energy due to friction.

 

Other systems show similar transformations. Electrical energy can become light and heat in a light bulb. Chemical energy in food can be transformed into mechanical energy when muscles move.

Scientists track these changes to observe how energy moves through systems.

 

Your mission is to report on this scientific discovery as a breaking news broadcast explaining how the Law of Conservation of Energy works in real-world systems.

🧰 Your Task

You will create a 1–2 minute maximum breaking news broadcast explaining the Law of Conservation of Energy.

 

Your report should explain:

• What energy is
• The Law of Conservation of Energy
• How energy can transfer between objects
• How energy can transform from one form into another

 

Your video should sound like a real science news report explaining an important discovery.

Step 1— Enter the Correct VR Location

1️⃣ Enter ENGAGE VR

 

2️⃣ Change your Group to: OAO Grade 7

⚠️ If you do not change your group, the correct location will not appear.

 

3️⃣ Load the OPTIMA News location

Your broadcast must be recorded from the OPTIMA News studio environment.

Step 2— Plan Your News Report

Your broadcast must explain the Law of Conservation of Energy and provide examples of energy transfers or transformations.

 

Your report should include:

• A clear explanation that energy cannot be created or destroyed

• At least one example of energy transfer

• At least one example of energy transformation

 

Examples you might explain include:

• A flashlight converting chemical energy into light and heat
• A moving object slowing down due to friction
• Electrical energy powering a light bulb
• Chemical energy in food allowing muscles to move

 

Your explanation should clearly show that energy changes form but is never lost.

 

Example opening:

“Good evening. This is EarthWatch News with a scientific breakthrough. Scientists report new observations that support the Law of Conservation of Energy, showing that energy cannot be created or destroyed…”

Step 3— Optional Broadcast Enhancements

To make your report feel more like a real news broadcast, you may add visual elements such as:

• Diagrams of energy transformations
• Images of scientific systems
• Graphics showing energy changing forms
• Studio decorations or background visuals

 

These additions can make your broadcast more realistic.

⚠️ These enhancements are optional and are NOT required for full credit.

 

Your grade will be based on the accuracy of your explanation, not decorations.

Step 4— Record Your Broadcast

Record a 1–2 minute maximum video inside the OPTIMA News location.

 

Your broadcast should:

• Explain the Law of Conservation of Energy
• Describe how energy can transfer or change forms
• Include at least one example of energy transformation or transfer
• Be clear, scientific, and easy for viewers to understand

 

You may present your report like a science reporter explaining an important discovery.

🌎 Required Components

Your video must include:

✔ Explanation of energy

✔ Explanation of the Law of Conservation of Energy

🧠 Putting AI to the Test: Energy Transformations

📜 Standard:
SC.7.P.11.3 – Recognize that energy can be transformed from one form to another, including electrical, mechanical, chemical, thermal, and radiant energy.

🎯 Objective

In this assignment, you will use an AI image generator to create a scientific diagram showing how energy transforms from one form into another within a system.

 

Energy is constantly changing form in the world around us. Every time something moves, produces heat, gives off light, or creates sound, energy is being transferred or transformed.

 

Scientists explain this principle using the Law of Conservation of Energy, which states that energy cannot be created or destroyed. Instead, energy can move between objects or change from one form into another.

 

Because energy transformations occur in nearly every physical process, scientists often study how energy moves through systems and what evidence shows that energy is conserved.

 

Examples of common energy transformations include:

• A flashlight converting chemical energy → electrical energy → light and thermal energy
• A toaster converting electrical energy → thermal energy
• A car converting chemical energy in fuel → mechanical energy
• A speaker converting electrical energy → sound energy

 

In each of these examples, the energy does not disappear. Instead, it changes form while the total amount of energy in the system remains constant.

 

In this assignment, you will put AI to the test by generating a visual model of an energy transformation system and evaluating how accurately the AI represents the science.

 

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

• Identify different forms of energy
• Explain how energy transforms from one form into another
• Recognize evidence that energy is conserved
• Evaluate whether an AI-generated scientific diagram accurately represents energy transformations

🌌 Mission Briefing

Scientists often study energy by examining systems, which are the objects or processes being investigated.

 

When scientists analyze a system, they track:

• The initial form of energy
• The energy transformations that occur
• The final forms of energy produced

 

Sometimes these final forms include heat, sound, light, or motion, which serve as evidence that energy has changed form rather than disappeared.

 

Your mission is to use AI as a scientific tool to generate a diagram showing how energy moves through a system. Then you will evaluate the results and determine whether the AI correctly represented the energy transformations.

🧰 Your Task

You will use an AI image generator to create a scientific diagram showing an energy transformation system.

 

You may use any AI image generator, including:

• Canva Magic Media
• ChatGPT image generator
• Grok
• Another AI tool of your choice

 

Your generated image should clearly show how energy changes from one form into another.

 

After generating the image, you will label the energy forms and explain the transformation.

Step 1 — Choose an Energy Transformation System

Select one real-world system where energy transforms from one form into another.

 

Examples include:

• Flashlight
• Toaster
• Speaker
• Car engine
• Battery-powered device
• Solar panel system
• Wind turbine
• Roller coaster

 

Your system must include at least two energy transformations.

 

Example:

Chemical Energy → Electrical Energy → Light Energy + Thermal Energy

Step 2 — Write Your AI Prompt

Before generating your image, write a clear prompt describing the scientific diagram you want the AI to create.

 

Your prompt should include:

• The system you are modeling
• The forms of energy involved
• Arrows showing energy transformations
• An educational science diagram style

 

Example prompts:

Flashlight Example:
“Scientific diagram showing energy transformations in a flashlight, chemical energy in the battery converting to electrical energy and then producing light energy and thermal energy, arrows showing energy flow, labeled educational diagram.”

 

Toaster Example:
“Educational science diagram of a toaster showing electrical energy converting into thermal energy that heats bread, arrows showing the energy transformation, labeled textbook-style diagram.”

 

Generate 2–3 images and choose the one that best represents the science.

 

⚠️ Important: The example prompts above are only examples to help you understand how prompts work.
You may NOT copy or use my prompt for your image.

 

You must create your own prompt using your own wording.

 

AI tools often generate very similar images when the same prompt is used, which makes it easy to identify copied prompts. If the same prompt is used, the images will look nearly identical and it will be clear that the example prompt was used.

 

Your goal is to construct your own prompt like a scientist giving instructions to a computer model.

Step 3 — Add Scientific Labels

Download your image and add at least four science labels showing the forms of energy in your system.

 

Examples of labels include:

• Chemical Energy
• Electrical Energy
• Mechanical Energy
• Thermal Energy
• Light Energy
• Sound Energy
• Energy Transformation
• Energy Transfer

 

Your diagram should clearly show how the energy changes form.

 

You may add labels using Canva, Google Slides, PowerPoint, or another drawing tool.

Step 4 — Explain the Energy Transformation

Write 4–6 sentences explaining:

• What system your diagram shows
• The initial form of energy in the system
• The energy transformations that occur
• Evidence showing that energy was conserved

 

Your explanation should clearly show that energy changed form but was not destroyed.

 

Be sure to spell check your writing and use proper grammar, capitalization, and punctuation before submitting.

🧠 Reflection Writing

Scientists evaluate tools and models to determine how accurately they represent scientific ideas.

 

Write a 4–6 sentence reflection explaining:

• Which AI tool you used
• Whether the AI diagram correctly showed the energy transformations
• Something the AI did well
• Something the AI did incorrectly or something you had to fix

 

You must also include your final AI prompt in this section so your teacher can see how you guided the AI to create your image.

 

Your reflection and prompt may be:

Remember to spell check your writing and use proper grammar and punctuation before submitting.

🎯 Objective

In this assignment, you will create a scientific energy log entry by drawing and explaining how energy is changing form in a survival situation.


Energy is constantly changing form in the world around us. These changes, called energy transformations, help explain how systems function.

 

Energy can change between forms such as mechanical, thermal, light, sound, electrical, and chemical energy.

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

An OPTIMA Science Comic Special Issue

📜 Standard:
SC.7.P.10.1 – “Illustrate that the Sun’s energy arrives as radiation with a wide range of wavelengths, consisting of visible light, infrared, and ultraviolet radiation.”

🎯 Objective
Independently create a science comic that explains how energy from the Sun travels as radiation and behaves across the electromagnetic spectrum.

 

Students will demonstrate understanding of how solar energy is transferred through space as waves by accurately modeling radiation, wavelength, and different types of electromagnetic energy using correct scientific vocabulary and clear cause-and-effect explanations.

 

Through this assignment, students will trace how energy leaves the Sun and travels through empty space as radiation. Students will explain how wavelength is related to energy and how different types of radiation—infrared, visible light, and ultraviolet—interact with Earth in different ways.

 

By the end of this assignment, students should be able to visually and scientifically explain how energy from the Sun travels as waves and why different wavelengths carry different amounts of energy.

🌌 Mission Briefing
The Sun is constantly sending energy across space.

But this energy does not travel in the way we might expect.

 

Instead of traveling through air or matter, this energy moves as radiation—waves that carry energy across millions of miles of empty space.

 

When this energy reaches Earth, it does not all behave the same way.

Some waves have long wavelengths and carry less energy.
Other waves have short wavelengths and carry much more energy.

 

Together, these waves form something powerful:

The electromagnetic spectrum.

 

Within this spectrum are different types of radiation that affect Earth in different ways.

 

Infrared radiation warms Earth’s surface.
Visible light allows us to see and supports life processes.
Ultraviolet radiation carries higher energy and can have stronger effects on living organisms.

 

Even the sunlight we see as white light is made up of many different colors, each with its own wavelength and energy.

 

Your mission is to take this invisible system and turn it into a clear, visual explanation.

 

You are not just creating a comic—you are modeling how energy travels, behaves, and affects Earth.

⚠️ Comic Focus: Read Carefully

This comic is a little different than the other comic editions we have created this year.

 

In this assignment, your focus is not just on storytelling—it is on the science behind what is happening.

 

You are using the comic book / graphic novel format as a tool to explain a scientific concept step-by-step.

 

Each panel should build on the previous one and clearly show how energy from the Sun travels as radiation and behaves across different wavelengths.

 

You are not just drawing a comic—you are modeling how energy moves through space and interacts with Earth.

🧰 Step 1: Comic Focus

Your comic must be a Scientific Breakdown.

 

🔬 Scientific Breakdown
Create a step-by-step science comic that explains how solar energy travels as radiation and how different wavelengths behave.

 

Your comic should feel like a visual explanation where each panel builds on the previous one.

 

Each panel must represent one part of the concept and connect to the next to form a complete chain of understanding.

✏️ Step 2: Comic Requirements

✅ 6 panels

Each panel must represent part of the scientific concept and connect clearly to the next. Your comic should show a clear progression from energy leaving the Sun to different types of radiation interacting with Earth.

🤖 AI Comic Expectations (Important)

If you choose to use AI to create your comic visuals, you are still responsible for the science, explanations, and accuracy of your work.

 

AI tools may help generate images, but they often create:

• Incorrect labels
• Misspelled or unreadable text

Because of this:

👉 You MUST make corrections and add your own captions, labels, and explanations

• Gibberish or unreadable words
• Incorrect vocabulary
• Missing or unclear explanations

 

➡️ It will lose points under Science Accuracy and Clarity

 

🧠 Remember:
AI is a tool — not the scientist.

 

YOU are responsible for explaining how radiation and wavelengths work.

📖 Step 3: What Your Comic MUST Explain

Your comic must include ALL of the following scientific ideas:

  1. ☀️ Radiation from the Sun
    Energy traveling from the Sun to Earth through empty space
  1. 🌌 Radiation as Waves
    Energy traveling in the form of waves
  1. ⚡ Wavelength and Energy Relationship
    Shorter wavelengths = higher energy
    Longer wavelengths = lower energy
  1. 🌡️ Infrared Radiation
    Longer wavelengths that are felt as heat
  1. 👁️ Visible Light and White Light
    Visible light is what we can see
    White light contains multiple colors (spectrum)
  1. ☢️ Ultraviolet Radiation and Light Separation
    Shorter wavelengths with higher energy
    Light can be separated into a spectrum (rainbow/prism)

Radiation

Spectrum

 

👉 Vocabulary must be used correctly and in context to count.

Every comic must clearly show that:

  • Energy from the Sun travels as radiation
  • Radiation travels in waves
  • Wavelength determines energy
  • Different wavelengths affect Earth in different ways
  • The electromagnetic spectrum includes multiple types of radiation

 

Your comic should clearly show this chain of understanding from beginning to end.

💡Light Lab: Investigating How Light Interacts with Matter

📜 Standard:
SC.7.P.10.2 – Observe and explain that light can be reflected, refracted, and/or absorbed.

🎯 Objective

In this assignment, you will step into the role of a scientist and design a working lab model in VR that demonstrates how light interacts with different materials.

Light is a form of energy that travels in waves and interacts with objects in different ways.

 

When light hits an object, it can:
• Reflect (bounce off)
• Refract (bend through)
• Absorb (turn into heat)

These interactions explain how we see, how lenses work, and how energy is transferred through light.

 

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

• Explain how light interacts with matter
• Identify reflection, refraction, and absorption
• Design a scientific model that demonstrates light behavior
• Use evidence and reasoning to explain what happens to light

🔦 Mission Briefing

The lab lights flicker.

A sharp beam of light cuts across the room—then bends, scatters, and vanishes into darkness.

 

Your console crackles to life.

“…Light Behavior Analysis Unit… do you copy…”

“We are losing control of our optical systems.”

 

Data floods your screen—light beams refracting unpredictably, reflections scattering in the wrong directions, energy readings spiking where absorption should not be occurring.

A second transmission overrides the first.

 

Critical technologies are beginning to fail:

• Imaging systems cannot focus
• Communication signals are breaking apart
• Energy systems are overheating
• Measurement tools are returning inconsistent data

 

Scientists rely on light to observe, measure, and understand the world. But right now, light is not behaving as expected—and no one knows why.

• Observations cannot be trusted
• Data cannot be confirmed
• Systems cannot be repaired

💡 Mission Reminder
Great scientists don’t just observe the world—they design experiments to understand it.

💡 Understanding Light Interactions (Examples)

Before you build, make sure you understand what each interaction looks like:

• Reflection (light bounces off a surface)
Example: Light hitting a mirror and bouncing back, allowing you to see your reflection

• Refraction (light bends when passing through a material)
Example: A straw appearing bent in a glass of water, or light passing through a lens

• Absorption (light energy is taken in and often converted into heat)
Example: Black pavement getting hot in the sun because it absorbs light energy

Your goal is to create a space where light can be:

assignments.html:
🎢 Wave World Experience: Designing an Educational Theme Park
📜 Standard:
SC.7.P.10.3 – Describe how waves can transfer energy through a medium.

🎯 Objective

In this assignment, you will step into the role of a designer and create your own educational theme park based on how waves move through different materials.

Waves are all around us and are responsible for many everyday experiences, including sound, light, and motion in water.

 

Because waves behave differently depending on the material they travel through:

• Some waves move faster in solids than in liquids or gases
• Light waves can travel through empty space, but sound waves cannot
• Waves transfer energy, not matter
• The medium affects how waves move and behave

 

By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

• Explain how waves move through different materials
• Connect science to real-world applications
• Describe how energy moves through waves
• Communicate ideas clearly through writing

🌊 Mission Briefing

As visitors enter your theme park, they are stepping into a world where energy is constantly moving and interacting with different materials. From the moment they arrive, they are surrounded by experiences that show how waves travel, change speed, and behave differently depending on what they move through.

 

This is not just an amusement park—it is a place where every ride, attraction, and detail is intentionally designed to teach something meaningful. Guests are not only there for excitement, but to understand how waves move through solids, liquids, gases, and even empty space in the case of light.

 

Throughout the park, visitors explore experiences that connect them to real-world science. They see how sound travels through air and solids, how light moves through space and materials, and how waves transfer energy without moving matter. Each attraction is built with purpose, helping guests make connections between what they experience and how waves behave in everyday life.

 

However, this park is still in development, and the design team is looking for new ideas that bring learning and creativity together.

 

You have been selected as part of the Wave World Design Team, and your role is to design a section of the park that is both engaging and educational. Your goal is to create an experience where visitors not only have fun, but leave with a deeper understanding of how waves can transfer energy through a medium.

🧰 Your Task

You will write a minimum of 3 paragraphs explaining your educational theme park.

 

Your response MUST include:

  • The name of your theme park (and how/why it got its name)
  • A description of the overall theme and purpose for your park
  • Your top 2 rides or experiences at the park (Make sure you explain what type of ride or experience they are, what they teach the public, what colors the ride is... try to give me so many details I can picture it!)
  • How your park educates the public about how waves can transfer energy through a medium
  • A description of creative food and drink options in your park
  • How your park helps people understand waves and energy transfer

 

Your writing should clearly explain how your park connects to what we learned this week.

💡 Writing Expectations

• Minimum of 3 paragraphs
• You may write more if you choose
• Use clear explanations and creative details
• Stay focused on the topic
• Make connections to real-world science
• Use proper spelling, grammar, and complete sentences

🧾 Submission Options

You may choose what works best for you:

• Handwrite in your science notebook
• Type and submit as a Word or Google Doc

🚨 Important Note

Comments on the assignment will NOT be counted for a grade.

Make sure your work is submitted properly.

⭐ Bonus Opportunity

Want to take your theme park to the next level?

You can earn +2 bonus points by creating a logo for your theme park.

 

Your logo should:

• Match the theme and name of your park
• Be creative and visually clear
• Represent the purpose of your park

 

You may choose how to create your logo:

• ✏️ Hand-drawn in your notebook
• 💻 Digitally created (Canva, Google Slides, etc.)
• 🤖 AI-generated (if you use AI, include your prompt)

 

💡 If you use AI, make sure your prompt clearly describes your theme park and design ideas.

📊 Rubric

Category Points What This Means

Creativity & Theme Park Design 5 Unique, engaging, and well-developed ideas
Writing Quality 5 Organized, clear paragraphs with complete explanations
⭐ Bonus: Theme Park Logo +2 Creative logo that matches the park’s theme and purpose

 

💯 This assignment is worth 20 Points (+2 Bonus Possible).
